course.title: ML for Beginners
course.subtitle: The classic 12-week tour of classical ML — pumpkins, cuisines, hotel reviews and power grids.
course.credit_line: Curriculum © Microsoft · MIT License · digested with credit, shared free.
course.after_note: The Data Science and AI for Beginners petals continue the line; then deep learning frameworks.

modules.title: Introduction
modules.blurb: What ML is, where it came from, and the fairness questions it drags along.

lessons.title: Introduction to machine learning
keys: ML: programs that learn patterns from data instead of being told the rules
Supervised (labeled), unsupervised (structure), reinforcement (reward)
Features in, model out, predictions onwards — the whole pipeline

lessons.title: The history of machine learning
keys: From statistics and perceptrons (1958) to deep learning winters and springs
Data + compute + algorithms: revolutions happen when all three move
Knowing the history explains today's vocabulary

lessons.title: Fairness and machine learning
keys: Biased data in, biased model out — math does not launder bias
Fairness definitions conflict; pick one and defend it
Unfairness is measurable: audit before and after training

lessons.title: Techniques for machine learning
keys: Regression predicts numbers, classification predicts labels, clustering finds groups
Model choice follows question shape, not fashion
Split data first: train / validation / test — and never peek

modules.title: Regression
modules.blurb: Predicting numbers, with North American pumpkin prices as the running dataset.

lessons.title: Tools of the trade — Python and Scikit-learn
keys: pandas for data, matplotlib for eyes, Scikit-learn for models
The Scikit-learn contract: fit(X, y) → predict(X)
Notebooks are for exploration; scripts are for repeats

lessons.title: Visualize and clean the data
keys: Plot first: distributions, scatter, outliers — models are blind, you aren't
Missing values: drop, impute, or flag — never ignore
Garbage in, gospel out is the most dangerous pipeline

lessons.title: Linear and polynomial regression
keys: Linear regression: the best straight line through the cost function
Polynomial curves fit harder shapes — and overfit harder too
R², MAE, RMSE: one number never tells the whole story

lessons.title: Logistic regression
keys: Logistic regression outputs probability, not a number
Sigmoid squashes the line into 0..1; threshold turns it into a decision
Despite the name, it's the baseline classifier

modules.title: The web app
modules.blurb: Ship the model: a trained predictor behind a web UI.

lessons.title: Build a web app to use your model
keys: A deployed model is worth ten notebooks
Save with pickle/joblib/ONNX, load server-side, serve predictions
Version the model with the app — they upgrade together

modules.title: Classification
modules.blurb: Labels, cuisines and recommenders — the most common ML shape.

lessons.title: Introduction to classification
lessons.objective: Clean, prep and visualize for classification.
keys: Classification predicts which bucket — binary, multiclass, multilabel
Class imbalance: accuracy lies; balance or reweight
Categorical features need encoding: one-hot usually first

lessons.title: Classifiers I — the cuisines dataset
keys: Start with logistic regression, then decision trees, then SVMs
Each classifier has a bias — a shape of problem it believes in
Cross-validation: trust the average, not the lucky split

lessons.title: Classifiers II — more classifiers
keys: Random forest: many weak trees vote into one strong model
k-NN: you are the average of your k nearest neighbors
Ensembles win Kaggle; single trees win explanations

lessons.title: Applied — a recommender web app
lessons.objective: Turn the classifier into a product.
keys: Recommenders are classification over 'will they like it?'
Cold start is the product problem hiding in the ML demo
Prediction serving shape: batch, on-demand, or stream

modules.title: Clustering
modules.blurb: Finding groups nobody labeled — Nigerian musical tastes as the dataset.

lessons.title: Visualize and prep for clustering
keys: No labels means no right answer — structure is the goal
Scale features first: distance metrics punish big numbers
Density plots and t-SNE give unsupervised eyes

lessons.title: K-Means clustering
keys: K-Means: pick k centroids, assign, move, repeat
The elbow method picks k where more clusters stop paying
Clusters describe, they don't explain — name them yourself

modules.title: Natural language processing
modules.blurb: Tea, translation and hotel reviews — language as data.

lessons.title: Introduction to NLP
lessons.objective: NLP basics by building a simple bot.
keys: NLP pipeline: normalize → tokenize → vectorize → model
Computers count words; meaning must be engineered in (or learned)
Even a rule-based bot teaches the pipeline

lessons.title: Common NLP tasks
keys: POS tagging, NER, stemming/lemmatization — the grammar layer
Bag-of-words and TF-IDF: frequency as meaning, first approximation
Vectors make text countable; counting makes text modelable

lessons.title: Translation and sentiment analysis
lessons.objective: Two workhorse tasks with Jane Austen.
keys: Sentiment: polarity scores from lexicons or learned classifiers
Translation was sequence-to-sequence's proving ground
Neutral text exists — and breaks naive sentiment models

lessons.title: Hotel reviews I
keys: Real reviews: slang, sarcasm, spam — the messy middle
Preprocessing choices dominate classical NLP results
Evaluate on held-out human labels, not vibes

lessons.title: Hotel reviews II
keys: Feature reduction kills noise and overfitting both
Confusion matrix: which class is the model lying about?
Iterate one variable at a time or learn nothing

modules.title: Time series
modules.blurb: Forecasting the future from the past — world power usage as the dataset.

lessons.title: Introduction to time series forecasting
keys: Time series: trend + seasonality + noise, decomposed
Never shuffle time: walk-forward validation, not random splits
Lag features turn forecasting into regression

lessons.title: Forecasting with ARIMA
keys: ARIMA = autoregression + integration (differencing) + moving average
Stationarity first: difference until the trend dies
ARIMA is a strong baseline that deep learning must beat

lessons.title: Forecasting with SVR
keys: SVR fits a tube around the data — errors inside the tube are free
Kernel choice is the whole game
Compare forecasters on the same horizon, fairly

modules.title: Reinforcement learning
modules.blurb: Peter, the wolf, and learning by consequence.

lessons.title: Introduction to reinforcement learning — Q-Learning
keys: RL: agent, environment, state, action, reward — the loop that learns by doing
Q-table: the learned value of every move in every situation
Explore vs exploit: sometimes try the worse move to learn better

lessons.title: Help Peter avoid the wolf — the Gym
keys: Gym gives environments; you give the policy
Rewards shape behavior — badly designed rewards shape bad behavior
Episodes, discounting, and patience: credit is delayed

modules.title: In the wild — postscript
modules.blurb: Real-world applications, and debugging models with the RAI dashboard.

lessons.title: Real-world ML scenarios and applications
keys: Most production ML is boring, classical, and immensely valuable
Finance, health, agriculture — the pumpkin pipeline scaled up
The hard part is data and deployment, not the model

lessons.title: Model debugging with the RAI dashboard
lessons.objective: Debug ML with Responsible AI tooling.
keys: Debugging ML = data slices, error analysis, feature attribution
Model cards document intent and limits — write one
A deployed model without monitoring is a time bomb
